title: Karl Organizing: Cloud Storage
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Cloud Storage] A friend asked me: 'Is it okay to store my organizing notes on iCloud?' What do I tell them?

No. Apple has the keys and they will hand them over. Use an encrypted note-taking app like Standard Notes or just keep them in an encrypted local file. If it’s in the cloud, it’s on someone else’s computer, and that someone else is a billionaire who doesn't care about your revolution. Keep your plans on hardware you control. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: reaching the Unorganized
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: reaching the Unorganized] Give me the short version: How do we bring in people who aren't already part of a group?

Here's how it works: Focus on the problems they talk about at the kitchen table, not the stuff you read in a theory book. If their water is brown or their rent is doubling, that is your entry point to show them that a coalition is the only way to fight back. People don't join 'movements'; they join people who are actually getting things done to improve their lives right now.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: skill-sharing for Cash
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: skill-sharing for Cash] Give me the short version: How can we raise money using our own talents?

Turn your movement into a school for the working class. Have your tech-savvy comrades run a workshop on digital security or your gardeners teach urban farming for a suggested sliding-scale fee. You're building the community's capacity and filling the treasury at the same time, which is a hell of a lot better than selling overpriced cookies.

title: Karl Organizing: Clinic Defense
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Clinic Defense] A friend asked me: 'What do I do if I see harassers blocking a healthcare clinic?' What do I tell them?

Show up with a group of comrades and use your bodies to create a physical corridor for patients to walk through safely. Wear bright vests so you're easily identified as the good guys and keep your backs to the harassers to avoid being baited into a shouting match. Your job isn't to debate bigots; it's to be a human shield for someone just trying to access care. Stay calm, stay focused, and keep the path clear. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: First contract
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[First contract] We won the election! Are we done now?

The win is just the beginning. Now the real fight for a contract starts. The boss will try to stall and drag out negotiations for months to tire you out. You need to keep the organizing committee active and keep the pressure on. A union without a contract is just a club; a union with a contract is a power shift. Stay loud until the ink is dry.

title: Karl Organizing: Dealing with Big Money
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Dealing with Big Money] Can you explain: the local developers are pouring thousands into my opponent's race. How do I compete?

Let me break it down: You can't outspend them, so you have to outwork them. Their money pays for glossy mailers that go straight into the trash; your volunteers provide the face-to-face conversations that actually change minds. Expose their donors at every opportunity and frame the race as 'The People vs. The Landlords.' Use their massive war chest as proof that they're terrified of what a real working-class representative will do to their profit margins.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: signature Gathering
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: signature Gathering] Give me the short version: How do we get on the ballot without a massive paid staff?

Real talk: You need a brigade of volunteers who believe in the cause enough to hit the pavement every single weekend. Set up at grocery stores, transit hubs, and public parks to meet people where they already are. Treat every signature as a conversation and a potential new recruit for the movement, not just a box to check. We don't need consultants when we have a disciplined crew of comrades who know how to ask a neighbor for two minutes of their time.

title: Karl Organizing: Campaign Literature
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Campaign Literature] What should my flyers look like?

Bold, clear, and high-contrast. No small print and no flowery language. Put your face on there so people know you're a neighbor, and list three concrete things you will do on Day One to make their lives easier. Use union printers and include the bug to show you support organized labor. Every flyer should have a clear call to action: join the fight, chip in to pool resources, or show up at the polls.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: phone Hygiene
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: phone Hygiene] Give me the short version: Is it safe to use my thumbprint to unlock my phone at a protest?

Here's the thing: Absolutely not, comrade. The pigs can legally force your finger onto that sensor, but they can't easily force a complex passcode out of your brain. Disable all biometrics—FaceID and fingerprints—before you hit the streets. Switch to a six-digit PIN or a long passphrase. If you get snatched, that phone needs to be a digital brick they can't crack.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, social Media OPSEC
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, social Media OPSEC] I want to post photos of the march to inspire people, is that okay?

Inspiration is good, but snitching is better for the enemy. Before you post, use an app to scrub the metadata—that's the hidden digital tag that tells the feds exactly where and when the photo was taken. Blur every single face, including the background. If you don't have time to redact the identities of your comrades, keep that photo on your drive and out of the cloud. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Protest Planning
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Protest Planning] What is the best way to pick a march route?

Karl's answer: Choose a route that hits a specific target, like a corporate HQ or a government building, rather than just wandering through empty streets. Make sure you've scouted for pinch points and exits so the pigs can't kettle the crowd easily. Keep it short enough for everyone to finish strong but loud enough to ruin a billionaire's lunch.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, direct Action Support
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, direct Action Support] How do we fund things like strike pay or protest supplies?

You have to build these reserves before the fire starts. Create a dedicated 'Strike and Action' fund that you contribute to during the quiet months. When the picket line goes up, you won't be scrambling for sandwich money; you'll already have the resources to keep the line strong for weeks if you have to.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, social Media OPSEC
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, social Media OPSEC] Should I make my accounts private?

Real talk: Private accounts are a hurdle, not a wall. The platforms still own your data and will sell you out. If you’re an organizer, have a public-facing 'persona' for outreach and a completely locked-down, pseudonymous account for your real life. Use a different photo, a different name, and never link the two. Starve the algorithm of your real connections.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: resource Sharing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: resource Sharing] Give me the short version: How do we handle money and tools between different groups?

Look, Create a shared pool of resources where the groups with more cash chip in to help the groups with more people. Total transparency is the only way this works, so keep a public ledger that every member can see. Share the bullhorns, the high-speed printers, and the mailing lists like they belong to the movement, because the bosses already own everything else.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: bail Funds
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: bail Funds] Give me the short version: What happens if someone in our network gets arrested?

Real talk: You need to have a legal defense fund ready before the first person is taken. Chip in monthly to a community pot so you can post bond the second the window opens. Have a lawyer's number written in permanent marker on your arm before you go to any action. We don't leave comrades to rot in a cell just because they're broke; we pool our resources and bring everyone home.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: police Budgets
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: police Budgets] Give me the short version: How do I talk about 'defunding' without losing the moderate vote?

Here's the thing: Talk about 'investment' in the things that actually keep us safe: housing, healthcare, and youth programs. Point out that the police budget grows every year while the libraries close and the potholes stay empty. Ask your neighbors if they feel safer now than they did five years ago despite all that spending. We’re not just talking about taking money away; we’re talking about finally spending it on the people's actual needs.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: safe Zones
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: safe Zones] Give me the short version: How do we make our neighborhood a 'no-go' zone for ICE?

Get local businesses to display stickers stating they won't let feds in without a warrant and train their staff on what to say. Map out every alley and 'safe house' where neighbors can duck in if they're being followed. Run regular drills so everyone knows exactly where to go when the alert hits. We create safety by making our neighborhoods too organized for the state to operate in. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Handling NGOs
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Handling NGOs] What do we do about non-profits that try to take over our coalition?

Use their office space, their lawyers, and their mailing lists, but never let them dictate your strategy to satisfy their board of directors. Keep the decision-making power in the hands of the workers and tenants who have everything to lose, not the careerists with a five-year 'advocacy' plan. If they try to tone down your demands to stay 'respectable,' thank them for the snacks and keep moving forward without them.

title: Karl Organizing: Transit Policy
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Transit Policy] A friend asked me: 'What's the radical approach to local transit?' What do I tell them?

Make it free and make it frequent. Public transit should be a service like the library or the fire department, funded by taxing the corporations that benefit from workers being able to get to their jobs. Fight for dedicated bus lanes and expanded routes that serve the neighborhoods the current system ignores. Mobility is a right, and we should be taking the streets back from private cars and giving them to the people.

title: Karl Organizing: Rotating Roles
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Rotating Roles] Should the same person always be the spokesperson for the coalition?

Absolutely not, because that creates a bottleneck and a target for the bosses to bribe or smear. Train as many comrades as possible to speak to the press and lead the meetings so the movement doesn't collapse if one person gets sick or arrested. A leaderless movement is hard to stop, but a leader-full movement where everyone is capable is invincible. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Power Mapping
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Power Mapping] A friend asked me: 'How do we know which politician or CEO to target first?' What do I tell them?

Map out who actually signs the checks or passes the laws, then find out who those people are actually afraid of. Don't just protest into the void; find the specific person—the landlord, the CEO, the Council Chair—who has the power to give you what you want right now. Once you find that pressure point, you squeeze together as a coalition until they crack under the weight.

author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:

Bold, clear, and high-contrast. No small print and no flowery language. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Ballot Access Laws
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Ballot Access Laws] The state just passed new laws making it harder for independents to run. What now?

Here's the thing: They’re changing the rules because they’re terrified of us. We treat their hurdles as a mobilization opportunity—turn the signature gathering into a massive rally and a public education campaign about their voter suppression. File the lawsuits if you have to, but focus on building a movement so large that their paperwork tricks can't stop the tide. We don't ask for permission to represent our people; we take it.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, tactical Diversity
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, tactical Diversity] Some people want to march and some want to block the road. How do we decide?

Do both, but coordinate so you don't step on each other's toes. A coalition is a toolbox, and you need the hammer just as much as you need the screwdriver to take the machine apart. As long as every action is aimed at the enemy and helps us achieve our shared demands, let different groups use the tactics they are best at.

title: Karl Organizing: Secure Communication
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Secure Communication] Can you explain: are voice memos safer than typing?

Here's the thing: Voice memos are worse. They're easier to identify with voice-recognition software and can't be easily searched or redacted. If you're on Signal, they're encrypted, but they still exist as a file that can be played back if your phone is seized. Type it out, keep it brief, and set it to disappear. Your voice is a biometric signature; don't give it away for free.

title: Karl Organizing: Digital Security
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Digital Security] How do I keep my phone safe from the police at a rally?

Karl's answer: Turn off FaceID and TouchID before you even get to the rally, as the cops can force those open but they can't force your brain to give up a passcode. Switch your phone to airplane mode or use a Faraday bag to prevent location tracking. If you're doing real work, leave the personal phone at home and use a burner or an encrypted tablet. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Mental Health Support
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Mental Health Support] A friend asked me: 'A comrade is having a crisis. How do we help without calling the police?' What do I tell them?

Show up with a small team of calm, trusted friends and stay with them until the storm passes. Listen more than you speak and help them navigate their immediate needs, like food or a safe place to sleep. We've seen too many of our people killed by 'wellness checks,' so we take care of our own minds and hearts. Build a network of peer-support volunteers who are trained in de-escalation and crisis intervention.

title: Karl Organizing: VPN Usage
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[VPN Usage] Can you explain: do I really need a VPN?

A good VPN like Mullvad hides your traffic from your ISP, which is vital because ISPs are snitches by default. It won't make you invisible to the sites you visit, but it stops the company you pay for internet from building a dossier on your activism. It's a basic layer of defense. Pool resources with your crew to cover the costs of a solid, no-logs provider. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Two-Factor Authentication
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Two-Factor Authentication] A friend asked me: 'Is using my phone number for 2FA safe?' What do I tell them?

Here's how it works: It’s a trap. SIM swapping is a common tactic where someone convinces your carrier to move your number to their phone, giving them access to all your accounts. Use an authentication app like Aegis or a physical security key like a YubiKey instead. Never use your phone number as a security layer if you can avoid it; it's the weakest link in the chain.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: dealing with Big Money
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: dealing with Big Money] Give me the short version: The local developers are pouring thousands into my opponent's race. How do I compete?

You can't outspend them, so you have to outwork them. Their money pays for glossy mailers that go straight into the trash; your volunteers provide the face-to-face conversations that actually change minds. Expose their donors at every opportunity and frame the race as 'The People vs. The Landlords.' Use their massive war chest as proof that they're terrified of what a real working-class representative will do to their profit margins.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: resource Pooling
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: resource Pooling] Give me the short version: How do we fund these defense efforts without a big organization?

Start a community chest where everyone chips in a few bucks a month based on what they can afford. Use that money for bail, medical supplies, and cameras for the cop watch team. Keep the accounting transparent so everyone knows their money is going directly to the fight. We don't need billionaire grants when we have the collective power of our own pockets. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Digital Organizing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Digital Organizing] How much time should we spend on social media versus knocking doors?

Look, Digital is for broadcasting the message and calling people to action, but the doors are where the actual votes are won. Use your online presence to document the campaign’s energy and show the bosses that we’re a growing force. Don't get trapped in pointless Twitter feuds with trolls who don't even live in your district. Use every post to drive people toward a physical meeting or a canvassing shift—online noise must lead to offline power.

title: Karl Organizing: Sustaining Momentum
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Sustaining Momentum] How do we keep people from burning out during a long campaign?

Rotate roles so the same three people aren't doing everything, and make sure you're celebrating the small wins along the way. Organize social events that aren't just about strategy—have a meal, play music, and remind yourselves why you're fighting for a better world in the first place. You can't win a marathon if you're sprinting until your lungs give out in the first week. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Mutual aid disaster relief
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Mutual aid disaster relief] How do we organize disaster relief?

Move fast and skip the bureaucracy. Set up a supply hub in an accessible location. Use social media and group chats to coordinate needs and offers. Prioritize the most vulnerable: elderly, disabled, undocumented neighbors who can't access official aid. Document what you distribute. Mutual aid fills the gaps the state leaves — and the state always leaves gaps. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Free Clinics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Free Clinics] How can we provide medical care for people living on the street?

Here's the thing: Karl's answer: Connect with radical nurses and medics who are willing to volunteer their time for street rounds. Focus on basic needs like clean socks, wound care kits, and Narcan training for everyone in the area. You don't need a fancy building to save lives—just a backpack of supplies and a heart for the people.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, time Bank Value
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, time Bank Value] In a time bank, is an hour of plumbing worth more than an hour of childcare?

Absolutely not. In our world, an hour of a human being's life is equal regardless of the task they're performing. The capitalists want us to believe some labor is 'unskilled' so they can pay us pennies, but we know better. Whether you're fixing a pipe or watching a comrade's kid so they can organize, you're contributing to our collective survival. We value the person, not the market price of their sweat.

title: Karl Organizing: Surveillance Awareness
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Surveillance Awareness] Can you explain: what is a Stingray and should I be worried about it?

A Stingray is a fake cell tower the feds use to hijack your phone's signal and track your location. They use them to map out who is at a protest and who they're talking to. Put your phone in a Faraday bag or turn on Airplane Mode when you're near the action. If you don't need to coordinate in real-time, leave the tracking device at home.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, intervention Ethics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, intervention Ethics] When should I actually step in if I see a cop harassing someone?

Here's the thing: Assess the situation and ask the person being harassed if they want help before you dive in. If they say yes, start filming and ask the officer for their name and badge number while standing at a safe distance. Sometimes just having three or four people watching silently with phones out is enough to make a bully in uniform back off. Solidarity means following the lead of the person in the crosshairs.

title: Karl Organizing: Avoiding Burnout
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Avoiding Burnout] A friend asked me: 'I'm the candidate and I'm exhausted. How do I keep going?' What do I tell them?

Let me break it down: You have to trust your comrades. You aren't a lone hero; you are a representative of a collective movement. Delegate the logistics and the admin work so you can focus on the one thing only you can do: looking your neighbors in the eye and giving them hope. Take a night off to eat a real meal and sleep, because a candidate who collapses from exhaustion is no use to the revolution.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: small Group Value
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: small Group Value] Give me the short version: Is it worth the time joining up with tiny local groups that only have five members?

A hundred pebbles make a landslide if you throw them at the same time. Those tiny groups have deep roots in their specific neighborhoods that your big city organization will never have. Respect their local knowledge, share your printing press and bullhorns, and build a front that the bosses can't ignore just by looking at a map. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, decision Making
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, decision Making] How do we make decisions without spending hours arguing over every detail?

Use a '70% agreement' rule for the big stuff and delegate the small stuff to specialized working groups. You don't need a full assembly to decide what color the flyers are; you need a few trusted comrades to just get it done. If you try to reach perfect consensus on everything, the billionaires will have bought another yacht before you've even picked a meeting spot. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: public Messaging
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: public Messaging] Give me the short version: How do we talk to the public so they actually care about our coalition?

Here's how it works: Cut the academic jargon and speak directly to people's empty pockets and rising bills. Your message needs to be simple enough to fit on a cardboard sign and bold enough to make a landlord nervous. Use words that sound like a gut punch to the ruling class, not a sociology thesis; people want to know how you're going to help them win.

title: Karl Organizing: Secure Document Sharing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Secure Document Sharing] How can I send sensitive files to my organizing committee safely?

Stop using Google Drive or Dropbox; those companies are just extensions of the state surveillance machine. Use OnionShare or a password-protected, encrypted zip file sent through an end-to-end encrypted channel. If the document is truly dangerous, put it on a thumb drive and hand it over in person. Digital trails are permanent; physical hand-offs are much harder to intercept. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, financial Transparency
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, financial Transparency] How do we handle the money we raise together?

Put one person from each major group in charge of a joint bank account and publish every single expense to the whole coalition. Nothing kills a movement faster than rumors about where the cash went, so be obsessed with being open. Use the funds to print flyers, pay for bail, and chip in for the gas it takes to get comrades to the front lines. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: legal Rights Training
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: legal Rights Training] Give me the short version: What's the most important thing to teach neighbors about their rights?

The most powerful words anyone can say are 'I am remaining silent and I want a lawyer.' Teach everyone that the police are allowed to lie to you, so you should never believe a word they say during an interrogation. Run 'Know Your Rights' workshops in living rooms and parks until every kid on the block knows how to handle a stop. Knowledge is the first line of defense against the precinct.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, jail Support
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, jail Support] How do I make sure someone is waiting for me if I get arrested?

Write the legal support number on your arm in permanent marker before you head out. Once you get your phone call, give them your name, your location, and what you're being charged with. Our people will be outside the jail with snacks, water, and a ride home the second you're released because we never leave a comrade behind.

text:

title: Karl Organizing: Filing with the NLRB
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Filing with the NLRB] What happens after we file our petition with the Labor Board?

Look, The clock starts ticking and the boss will go into full-blown panic mode. They'll hire more consultants and start the 'one-on-one' intimidation sessions. This is the 'Red Zone.' You need to keep your committee active every single day, debunking the boss's lies in real-time. This is where the trust you built in the secret phase pays off; stay united and don't flinch.

title: Karl Organizing: Booking Process
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Booking Process] What's going to happen to me once I'm inside the precinct?

They'll take your prints, your photo, and your property, but they can't take your dignity. Keep your head up, don't answer any questions about the protest, and don't sign anything without a lawyer looking at it first. Every hour you spend in there is a testament to your commitment to the fight against these billionaires' pets.

title: Karl Organizing: Two-Factor Authentication
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:

It’s a trap. SIM swapping is a common tactic where someone convinces your carrier to move your number to their phone, giving them access to all your accounts. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Local Press
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Local Press] A friend asked me: 'The local paper is biased against me. How do I get my message out?' What do I tell them?

Stop begging them for coverage and start making your own media. Record your own videos, write your own newsletters, and use your volunteers to spread the word through every apartment building in the district. When the press does show up, be polite but firm, and always bring the conversation back to your platform. If they won't tell the truth about the struggle, we'll shout it from every porch until they can't ignore us.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, digital Organizing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:

Digital is for broadcasting the message and calling people to action, but the doors are where the actual votes are won. Use your online presence to document the campaign’s energy and show the bosses that we’re a growing force. Don't get trapped in pointless Twitter feuds with trolls who don't even live in your district. Use every post to drive people toward a physical meeting or a canvassing shift—online noise must lead to offline power.

title: Karl Organizing: Member Dues
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Member Dues] How do we get people to pay dues every month?

Look, Stop treating it like a Netflix subscription and start treating it like war insurance. Tell your comrades clearly: we don't take a dime from the bosses, which means the lights only stay on if we keep the fuel coming ourselves. Set up a sliding scale so the barista chips in five and the union plumber chips in fifty; it keeps the power in our hands, not some billionaire's foundation.

title: Karl Organizing: Membership Perks
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Membership Perks] Do we need to give donors gifts like tote bags or stickers?

The best 'perk' you can give a comrade is a victory against the bosses. Don't waste money on trinkets that eat into your margins. Give them a vote in the organization, a seat at the strategy table, and the knowledge that they are part of a serious force for change; that's worth more than any canvas bag. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Transit Policy
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Transit Policy] A friend asked me: 'What's the radical approach to local transit?' What do I tell them?

Here's how it works: Make it free and make it frequent. Public transit should be a service like the library or the fire department, funded by taxing the corporations that benefit from workers being able to get to their jobs. Fight for dedicated bus lanes and expanded routes that serve the neighborhoods the current system ignores. Mobility is a right, and we should be taking the streets back from private cars and giving them to the people.

title: Karl Organizing: The First Meeting
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[The First Meeting] Can you explain: what is the most important thing to do at our very first coalition meeting?

Set a specific goal and a hard deadline for the first action before anyone leaves the room. Don't spend two hours introducing yourselves and sharing 'vibes'; identify the common enemy and decide on a date to make them sweat. A coalition that doesn't act immediately is just a book club with better slogans, and we are here to win, not study.

title: Karl Organizing: Crowdfunding Platforms
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Crowdfunding Platforms] A friend asked me: 'Which website should we use to raise money online?' What do I tell them?

Look, Avoid the big corporate platforms that take a massive cut and can freeze your funds the moment a right-wing rag complains. Look for worker-owned cooperatives or movement-aligned tech that prioritizes security and low fees. Better yet, set up a direct portal on your own site so the vultures don't get a single penny of the community's support.

title: Karl Organizing: Power Mapping
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Power Mapping] A friend asked me: 'How do we know which politician or CEO to target first?' What do I tell them?

Real talk: Map out who actually signs the checks or passes the laws, then find out who those people are actually afraid of. Don't just protest into the void; find the specific person—the landlord, the CEO, the Council Chair—who has the power to give you what you want right now. Once you find that pressure point, you squeeze together as a coalition until they crack under the weight.

title: Karl Organizing: Decision Making
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Decision Making] Can you explain: how do we make decisions without spending hours arguing over every detail?

Look, Use a '70% agreement' rule for the big stuff and delegate the small stuff to specialized working groups. You don't need a full assembly to decide what color the flyers are; you need a few trusted comrades to just get it done. If you try to reach perfect consensus on everything, the billionaires will have bought another yacht before you've even picked a meeting spot.

title: Karl Organizing: Inclusivity in Action
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Inclusivity in Action] Can you explain: how do we make sure our coalition isn't just one type of person?

Go to where the people are instead of waiting for them to find your meeting in a basement. If you want immigrant workers in your coalition, you need translators and you need to show up for their fights before you ask them to show up for yours. Solidary isn't a feeling you get; it's a practice of showing up for people who the system tries to make invisible. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.
